notes: In response to a question from the Committee, Craig Dyer, Commissioner of Corporate Services/Chief Financial Officer, stated that from a property tax ratio perspective and in accordance with the Municipal Property Assessment Corporation (MPAC) and the Municipal Act, there is no ability to differentiate between affordable units and full market value, and that there is no ability from a property tax ratio perspective to put affordable or not-for-profit multi-residential properties in a different class and tax them at a different rate.

items.title: COR-CFN-23-020, 2022 Plan Update and Year End Financial Results
notes:
Bruce Lauckner, Chief Administrative Officer, introduced the report. Connie MacDonald, Chief Communications & Strategy Officer, spoke to the key initiatives, the Regional yearbook, Grand River Transit (GRT), affordable housing, and the 2023-2027 strategic plan. C. Dyer spoke to the year end financial results and indicated that the Region of Waterloo ended 2022 with a consolidated budget surplus of $7.2 million and that Waterloo Regional Police Services (WRPS) ended the year with a $0.3 million. He further noted that year-end surpluses and shortfalls will be allocated to or funded from Regional reserves in accordance with the Surplus Allocation Policy. He further spoke to the water and wastewater budgets and next steps. The financial results set out in this report will be reflected in the Region’s year-end financial statements, which will be submitted to Audit Committee on April 26, 2023.

In response to questions from the committee, Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering & Environmental Services, provided clarification on the variance in wastewater treatment, noting that the variance is a reflection of the previous dry summer, the surplus in water, and the increase in chemical cost for treatment. She further indicated that the increase in chemical cost and weather were taken into account for the budgeting this year.

In response to questions from the committee, C. Dyer stated that the 2023 approved budget contemplates approximately $8 million of transfers from the tax stabilization reserve into the 2023 operating budget. He further noted that if the Region was in a situation where the entire amount of the tax stabilization reserve was utilized over the course of the year, staff would review opportunities across the organization to offset the variance, and further noted there are available funds in other reserves that could be available if a situation of that magnitude presented itself. He further responded that there will be a review of the reserves and reserve fund policy during this term of Council

motions.item_title: COR-CFN-23-018, 2023 Property Tax Policy and Rates
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to 2023 property tax policies and rates as set out in Report COR-CFN-23-018 dated April 4, 2023: Establish the following property class tax ratios for the 2023 property tax year: Residential and New Multi-residential 1.0000 Multi-residential, Commercial and Industrial 1.9500 Landfill 1.5400 Pipeline 1.1613 Farmland and Managed Forest 0.2500 Direct staff to prepare the necessary by-laws to establish the 2023 property class tax ratios and the resulting 2023 Regional property tax rates for Regional Council’s consideration on April 19, 2023; Direct staff to report back in 2023 with a review of options for the multi-residential property class ratio in 2024 and beyond; and Notify the Area Municipalities within Waterloo Region accordingly.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to 2023 property tax policies and rates as set out in Report COR-CFN-23-018 dated April 4, 2023:

  1. Establish the following property class tax ratios for the 2023 property tax year:

    Residential and New Multi-residential  1.0000

     Multi-residential, Commercial and Industrial  1.9500

     Landfill     1.5400

     Pipeline    1.1613

     Farmland and Managed Forest 0.2500

  2. Direct staff to prepare the necessary by-laws to establish the 2023 property class tax ratios and the resulting 2023 Regional property tax rates for Regional Council’s consideration on April 19, 2023;
  3. Direct staff to report back in 2023 with a review of options for the multi-residential property class ratio in 2024 and beyond; and
  4. Notify the Area Municipalities within Waterloo Region accordingly.

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the 2022 Plan Update and Year End Financial Results as set out in report COR-CFN-23-020 dated April 4, 2023:
